correctness.rationale: For Z zeros, K ones, and surplus s=Z-(n-1), a marker at zero-rank a covers exactly [a-s,a] clipped to [0,n-1]. Covering all offsets requires K(s+1)≥n, and the host restriction gives Z≤2(K+1). For n≥4, s=0 is strictly too expensive; s=1 gives the asserted lower bound; s≥2 can attain it only at s=2 for odd n. At even length, the s=1 intervals must tile the target offsets in pairs. At odd length the s=2 word saturates all zero runs; at s=1 the first and last ranks must lie in {0,1} and {2m,2m+1}, respectively, and each gap is at most two. The feasible endpoint differences 2m and 2m-1 give precisely two end variants and the m single-short-gap variants. Each listed word meets the host constraint, covers the target offsets, has the required length, and in fact avoids 11. The boundary n=4 is included.
residual_risks: Separate exhaustive replay checked 41,384 hosts for 4≤n≤10 and complete optimizer sets; it does not certify the reported run through n=14 or replace the general proof. No formal proof or expert attestation is inferred.

value.rationale: A forbidden host factor changes the optimum for the natural all-offset, one-marker test family. The exact equality classification explains the parity effect and distinguishes the saturated zero runs from the near-tiling cases, supplying an explicit benchmark for constrained supersequence theory rather than a small-instance census.
